assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amination into a general, predictable bond-forming reaction. Its effect on pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis is very broad, and ligand design plus mechanistic work gave a clear and lasting framework.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic method and the ligand and mechanistic basis. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a precursor, so priority could be argued, but the broadly enabling chemistry is credited most fairly to Buchwald and Hartwig.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of heavy industrial use and independent confirmation. Recognition is timely, with the 2010 cross-coupling prize being a different bond type, so this is not duplicative.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would credit Kosugi as a third laureate or treat his work as a precursor.
My knowledge of the earliest priority details is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Direct TEM observation of multiwalled carbon nanotubes with their helical structure opened an entire field of nanocarbon science and materials. This is a structure-defined material with real applications, and electron microscopy was central to its discovery.
assessment.attribution: Iijima's 1991 Nature report is the decisive discovery. Endo's earlier vapor-grown fibers and Bethune's single-wall work (concurrent with Iijima) complicate priority, but a single-laureate or Iijima-led configuration is defensible.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of confirmation and application. Timing is late but not stale, and the prize has already recognized fullerenes and graphene.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over earlier hollow carbon filaments (Endo and others).
Whether chemistry or physics is the natural home for this discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The nanocrystalline mesoporous TiO2 dye-sensitized cell showed efficient molecular-based photovoltaics and opened a design space of interfacial charge transfer in porous nanostructured materials.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 O'Regan and Grätzel paper is the clear core, with Grätzel as intellectual leader. Hagfeldt's contributions are important but later and more developmental, so a two-person configuration is the cleanest.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced worldwide and mature, with commercial niche use. Commercial efficiency was later surpassed by perovskites, which weakens the case for urgency but not for originality.
uncertainties: Limited commercial impact compared with silicon.
Whether Hagfeldt should be included is an unresolved allocation question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas (M41S, MCM-41, SBA-15 and later routes) established a new family of materials with tunable 2-50 nm pores, supporting catalysis, adsorption and nanocasting. This is a major step in porous materials design, and I know the structural characterization well.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck at Mobil made the original M41S discovery, Ryoo extended it to ordered carbons and pore control, and Zhao and Stucky developed the SBA family. The credit is broad and contested, so any three-person selection leaves out a deserving person.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with thousands of confirming studies. Its role was partly displaced by zeolites, MOFs and COFs, and the 2025 prize recognized another porous-framework class.
uncertainties: Allocation among Mobil inventors and academic groups (Stucky, Zhao, Ryoo, Inagaki) is unclear.
Possible perception that the prize area was recently covered by the 2025 MOF recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new pharmacological modality that uses the ubiquitin-proteasome system, with mechanistic understanding (cereblon as the thalidomide target) and many clinical programs.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and developed PROTACs, and Ciulli provided structural and mechanistic design principles including VHL ligands. The molecular glue branch (Handa, Ito, Gray) is a separate and equally strong story, so the full credit does not fit within three people.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is accumulating but no approved PROTAC drug yet exists, so the impact is still ahead of the evidence. This is likely early.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug at the time of my knowledge.
Compound discovery: PROTAC and molecular glue contributions may need separate recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another without double-strand breaks, a conceptually elegant chemical approach to precise genome editing with strong therapeutic prospects.
assessment.attribution: Liu's lab conceived and built cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as first authors of the key papers. Whether a prize would credit the trainees, or only Liu, is an open question. Nishida and Kondo made a parallel cytidine deaminase editor.
assessment.maturity: About a decade old with early clinical use. Recognition is plausible but may be premature, and genome editing already received the 2020 prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the CRISPR prize for the genome-editing theme.
Credit among Liu, trainees and the Nishida-Kondo group.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers delivered an extraordinary efficiency rise in a very short time and created a large research area connecting materials chemistry and photophysics.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell, Park and Snaith drove the solid-state efficiency breakthroughs, and Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis were also important. Credit is crowded with real tension between priority and impact.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is well confirmed, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and scalability are unresolved. This is probably premature for chemistry.
uncertainties: Stability and commercial viability remain unproven.
Crowded attribution and uncertain priority between early reports.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at XFELs enabled structure determination from micro- and nanocrystals at room temperature with time-resolved capability, a methodological advance I value highly, related in spirit to my own work on nanocrystals.
assessment.attribution: Chapman, Fromme and Hajdu are central to the 2011 proof-of-principle with Photosystem I nanocrystals. Schlichting's contributions to time-resolved work and later applications are also strong, so credit is not settled.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed across facilities, but it relies on a small number of large instruments and the chemically transformative results are still emerging. Timing is probably early.
uncertainties: Whether the main impact has been methodological or has yet produced widely accepted new chemistry.
Competing nanocrystal methods like microED and 3D ED may reduce its uniqueness.
